lead.headline: Liquid Network's $320M White-Hat Pause Exposes Sidechain Security Model as Ethereum Consolidation Accelerates
lead.tldr: The Liquid Network halt and Harmony's proposed L1 shutdown show infrastructure fragmentation becoming economically untenable, while tokenized settlement and regulatory reopening signal where institutional capital is actually repricing.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, today the infrastructure layer is being stress-tested in public: two networks face existential decisions while settlement rails and regulatory frameworks harden around the survivors.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin sidechain Liquid pauses after purported ‘white hats’ withdraw $320M in BTC
top_signals.summary: The Bitcoin sidechain Liquid Network has paused operations following the withdrawal of approximately 4,000 BTC by individuals claiming to be white hat hackers. The actors have pledged to return the majority of the funds once the vulnerability is patched.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The 'white hat' withdrawal of 4,000 BTC from a federated sidechain controlled by a consortium of exchanges reveals that trusted-party architectures carry contingent liability risk that institutional treasuries will increasingly underwrite against, particularly as the pledged return remains unverified and the pause duration undefined.

top_signals.title: Citi, DBS complete first weekend tokenized cross-border deposit on Swift
top_signals.summary: Citi and DBS have successfully completed the first weekend cross-border deposit using Swift's blockchain ledger. This milestone demonstrates how tokenization can bypass traditional banking hours to enable 24/7 settlement.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Citi and DBS completing weekend settlement via Swift's blockchain ledger demonstrates that tokenized deposits are moving from pilot to operational utility, which reprices the competitive moat for neobanks and crypto-native settlement layers that have built 24/7 as their core value proposition.

top_signals.title: Harmony proposes shutting down layer 1, migrating ONE to Ethereum24m, Harmony proposes shutting down layer 1, migrating ONE to EthereumHarmony proposed sunsetting its layer-1 blockchain and migrating ONE to Ethereum, weeks after an exploit led to plans to discard 109,000 transactions.
top_signals.summary: Harmony has proposed shutting down its native layer-1 blockchain and migrating the ONE token to Ethereum. This move follows a recent exploit that necessitated the discarding of over 100,000 transactions.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Harmony's proposed migration to Ethereum after discarding 109,000 transactions validates the rollup-centric roadmap thesis that standalone L1s without differentiated execution or distribution face terminal capital flight, and we expect similar consolidation announcements from mid-tier networks within 12-18 months.

top_signals.title: UK financial watchdog weighs lifting prediction markets ban: Report10m, UK financial watchdog weighs lifting prediction markets ban: ReportCompanies offering binary options for retail investors have been barred from selling, marketing and distributing products in the UK since 2019 following a directive from the FCA.
top_signals.summary: The UK's Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) is reportedly considering lifting the ban on prediction markets and binary options for retail investors. This move would reverse a restrictive directive that has been in place since 2019.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The FCA's reconsideration of the 2019 prediction markets ban creates a regulatory path for Polymarket-class platforms to enter UK retail, which would reprice the addressable market for on-chain event contracts and likely accelerate compliance infrastructure spend ahead of the 2026 election cycle.

top_signals.title: Ethereum Foundation names 2 ‘must ship’ EIPs for Hegotá upgrade28m, Ethereum Foundation names 2 ‘must ship’ EIPs for Hegotá upgradeEthereum’s Hegotá upgrade will center on FOCIL and Frame Transactions as developers weigh dozens of other proposed changes for inclusion.
top_signals.summary: The Ethereum Foundation has identified FOCIL and Frame Transactions as the two essential Ethereum Improvement Proposals (EIPs) for the upcoming Hegotá upgrade. While dozens of other changes are being considered, these two are designated as 'must ship' for the network's evolution.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The Ethereum Foundation's prioritization of FOCIL and Frame Transactions for Hegotá signals that base-layer throughput and censorship resistance remain the non-negotiable investment criteria, even as L2 execution dominates user-facing activity.

deals.summary: Antarctic Exchange, a high-performance decentralized perpetuals exchange, has successfully raised $7 million in funding. The round was supported by investors including Valisa Capital Markets, Lucidity Capital, and Republic Crypto.

on_the_radar.title: ‘Oh, my God! Bro, bro, I’m going to spaz out!’ The first Bitcoin RICO case comes for a DOJ that gutted its ability to build it
on_the_radar.summary: A 22-year-old Singaporean dropout is facing the first Bitcoin-related RICO case after allegedly stealing $240 million. The case highlights the DOJ's efforts to prosecute large-scale digital asset theft despite internal resource challenges.

on_the_radar.title: South Korea's Hanwha develops tokenized securities platform on Avalanche as local regulation takes shape: report
on_the_radar.summary: South Korean conglomerate Hanwha is developing a tokenized securities platform utilizing the Avalanche blockchain. This move aligns with new local regulations that integrate tokenized securities into the national financial system starting next February.

on_the_radar.title: Philippines eyes payment operator registration freeze, tighter VASP checks
on_the_radar.summary: The Philippine central bank is proposing a one-year freeze on new payment operator registrations. Additionally, the regulator intends to implement stricter oversight and controls for arrangements involving Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs).

on_the_radar.title: Coldcard third-wave attacker moves 45% of stolen Bitcoin
on_the_radar.summary: An attacker involved in the third wave of thefts targeting Coldcard has moved 45% of the stolen Bitcoin. The funds were routed through THORChain and CoinJoin transactions to obscure the trail.

on_the_radar.title: Sanctum Flips Jupiter
on_the_radar.summary: Sanctum has surpassed Jupiter to become the leader in Total Value Locked (TVL) on the Solana network. This shift indicates a growing preference for Sanctum's liquid staking infrastructure within the ecosystem.

on_the_radar.title: Polish prosecutors charge suspect in Zondacrypto probe, seek pretrial detention
on_the_radar.summary: Polish prosecutors have officially charged Roman Ż. with organized crime and misappropriation as part of an investigation into Zondacrypto. Authorities are currently seeking pretrial detention for the suspect.

on_the_radar.title: Bitcoin holds near $80,000 despite renewed Fed rate hike fears as CPI test looms
on_the_radar.summary: Bitcoin is maintaining its price level near $80,000 despite increased market fears regarding a potential Federal Reserve rate hike in September. Investors are closely monitoring upcoming U.S. CPI inflation data for further direction.

on_the_radar.title: Fomo overtakes Pump.fun in daily revenue on Solana10m
on_the_radar.summary: Fomo has surpassed Pump.fun in terms of daily revenue on the Solana network. This indicates a shift in user preference or competitive dynamics within the Solana-based meme coin launchpad sector.

linkedin_post:
Two networks froze or folded today. Different reasons, same pressure.

Liquid's federated sidechain stopped block production after 4,000 BTC left through a hole the 'white hats' are still describing. Harmony proposed killing its L1 entirely, migrating ONE to Ethereum, weeks after it had to erase 109,000 transactions to contain an exploit. These are not bugs to patch. They are structural questions about who bears the liability when trusted infrastructure fails.

We underwrite infrastructure on continuity risk. Liquid's consortium model just demonstrated a coordination failure mode that a permissionless chain does not have. Harmony's sunset proposal is the first of several we expect from L1s that raised at layer-1 valuations without layer-1 differentiation.

The repricing is already visible in where capital is moving. Citi and DBS settled cross-border deposits over a weekend using Swift's tokenized ledger. Not a crypto-native rail. An incumbent rail, rebuilt. That is the competition now. 24/7 settlement is becoming table stakes, and the firms that can deliver it within existing compliance frameworks are widening their moat.

The FCA considering a reversal of its 2019 prediction markets ban adds another vector. If UK retail opens to on-chain event contracts, the compliance cost of a license becomes a barrier that favors scaled platforms over startup competitors.

What confirms the thesis: a second mid-tier L1 announcing migration by Q3. What kills it: Liquid resuming with unchanged federation architecture and no material outflow of BTC to self-custody alternatives.

We are watching the former more closely.
